prompt: Players fall through the platforms. Fix it by putting the platforms on collision layer 2 and adding layer 2 to the player's collision mask, with movement done in _process.

config.plan_model: Agent-tool model parameter 'sonnet' (Claude Code sub-agent; the harness did not report the resolved model id)
config.how: one fresh general-purpose sub-agent per plan, reads a job file with project brief + the developer prompt, writes numbered plan (<=8 steps, no code) via Write; not Claude Code plan mode

plans.text:
1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer's physics layer settings to confirm the current collision layer and mask on the platforms and ground, and check whether the tileset actually has a physics layer with collision polygons on the platform tiles.
2. Inspect the Player's CollisionShape2D and its current collision layer and mask, and review player.gd to see how movement is currently done (including any use of move_and_slide and gravity).
3. Set the platform tiles' physics layer so the TileMapLayer sits on collision layer 2, leaving the ground's setup consistent with that decision (or noting if ground should stay on its current layer).
4. Add layer 2 to the Player's collision mask while keeping its existing mask bits, so it still collides with whatever it collided with before.
5. Move the movement logic in player.gd from the physics callback into _process as requested, keeping gravity and velocity handling intact. Flag to the developer that CharacterBody2D movement normally belongs in _physics_process, since frame-rate-dependent movement in _process can cause tunneling and jitter, and could itself be a cause of falling through platforms.
6. Check the two enemy scenes for collision layers and masks, and adjust their masks to include layer 2 if they need to stand on the platforms too.
7. Run level_01.tscn and test walking, jumping and landing on every platform, including thin one-way platforms and edges, to confirm the player no longer falls through.
8. Report the changes made, and recommend moving movement back to _physics_process if any tunneling or inconsistent behavior remains at varying frame rates.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer, and confirm the platform tiles currently have a physics layer defined in the TileSet with collision polygons. Note the existing collision layer and mask values on the TileMapLayer, Player, and both enemy scenes so nothing is changed by accident.
2. Set the TileMapLayer's collision layer to layer 2 only, leaving ground behavior intact (or confirm whether ground should stay on its current layer). Make sure the TileSet's physics layer actually has collision shapes on the platform tiles, since a missing shape would also cause falling through.
3. Select the Player's CharacterBody2D and add layer 2 to its collision mask while keeping its existing mask bits. Leave the Player's own collision layer unchanged.
4. Check the two enemy scenes and decide whether they also need layer 2 in their masks so they stand on the platforms. Apply the same mask change only if they currently fall through too.
5. Open player.gd and move the movement logic from its current callback into _process, as the developer requested. Keep the move-and-slide call and gravity handling together so behavior stays consistent.
6. Account for the fact that _process runs at the variable render frame rate while physics bodies are meant to be driven from _physics_process. Scale velocity and gravity by delta, and tell the developer this may cause jitter or inconsistent collisions at varying frame rates, offering to revert to _physics_process if problems appear.
7. Run level_01.tscn and test landing on, walking along, and jumping up through platforms, plus the enemies' behavior, at different frame rates if possible. Verify the player no longer falls through and that ground collision still works.
8. Report what was changed (layers, masks, script callback) and any caveats, such as the _process concern, back to the developer.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer's physics settings to confirm the platforms currently have collision shapes and see which layer and mask they use. Also check player.gd and the Player node's layer and mask to understand why the player falls through.
2. Set the TileMapLayer's collision layer to layer 2 (and clear it from the layer it was on, if that's not wanted), making sure the tileset's physics layer actually has collision polygons on the platform tiles.
3. On the Player CharacterBody2D, add layer 2 to the collision mask while keeping the existing mask bits (such as the ground layer) enabled.
4. Check the two enemy scenes' masks and layers so that moving the platforms to layer 2 doesn't make the enemies fall through or stop colliding. Add layer 2 to their masks if they should stand on platforms.
5. Update player.gd so movement runs in _process as requested, keeping the move-and-slide call and gravity handling there. Note that physics bodies are normally moved in _physics_process, so flag to the developer that this may cause jitter or inconsistent collisions, and use delta so speed stays frame-rate independent.
6. Name layer 2 (for example "platforms") in the project's layer names settings so the setup is readable.
7. Run level_01.tscn and test walking, jumping, and landing on platforms at different frame rates, plus the enemies' behavior on the same platforms.
8. If falling through persists or movement feels unreliable, report back with findings and suggest moving movement to _physics_process as a follow-up, leaving that decision to the developer.

2. Set the TileMapLayer's collision layer to layer 2 for the platforms, making sure the tileset's physics layer is actually defined and the platform tiles have collision polygons. Keep the ground on its existing layer unless it should share layer 2.
3. Edit the Player's CharacterBody2D so its collision mask includes layer 2 in addition to any layers it already uses, without removing the existing bits.
4. Check the two enemy scenes and any other bodies that should or should not collide with layer 2, and adjust their masks only if the platform change affects them.
5. Open player.gd and move the movement logic into _process as requested. Flag to the developer that CharacterBody2D movement with move_and_slide normally belongs in _physics_process, because _process runs at a variable frame rate and can cause tunneling or inconsistent collisions, which may be a cause of the falling through.
6. If delta-dependent movement now runs in _process, make sure velocity and gravity are scaled by delta consistently so speed does not change with frame rate.
7. Run level_01.tscn and test landing on, walking along, and jumping up through each platform type, at different frame rates if possible, and confirm the player no longer falls through.
8. Verify enemies and ground still behave correctly, then summarize the changes and the _process caveat for the developer, offering to switch back to _physics_process if tunneling persists.

3. Open the Player's CharacterBody2D collision settings and add layer 2 to its collision mask, keeping any existing mask bits (such as ground and enemies) enabled.
4. Check both enemy scenes' masks and layers, so the new layer 2 assignment does not break enemy-vs-platform behavior or make enemies fall through too. Add layer 2 to their masks if they should walk on platforms.
5. Open player.gd and move the movement and gravity logic from its current callback into _process, as requested. Flag the concern that physics-body movement normally belongs in _physics_process because _process runs at a variable frame rate, which can cause tunneling and inconsistent collision, and mention it to the developer.
6. Make sure move_and_slide still runs after velocity is updated in the new location, and that delta is applied consistently so jump and gravity feel unchanged.
7. Run level_01.tscn and test walking, jumping, and landing on each platform type, plus the ground, at different frame rates if possible. Confirm the player no longer falls through.
8. Report the outcome to the developer, including the layer 2 setup, the _process caveat, and a recommendation to revert to _physics_process if jitter or tunneling appears.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer's TileSet to confirm that the platform tiles actually have physics shapes defined and note which collision layer they currently use. This identifies why the player falls through before anything is changed.
2. In the TileSet's physics layer settings, set the platform tiles' collision layer to layer 2 (leaving ground as it is unless it should share the layer), and verify each platform tile has a collision polygon.
3. Select the Player node and enable layer 2 in its collision mask, keeping its existing mask bits so it still collides with ground and anything else it did before.

5. Open player.gd and move the movement logic into _process as the developer requested. Because _process runs at a variable frame rate and move_and_slide is meant for the physics step, flag this tradeoff to the developer and scale motion by delta so speed stays consistent.

7. Run level_01.tscn and test landing on, walking along, and jumping onto the platforms and the ground, plus enemy interactions, at both normal and low frame rates.
8. If the player still falls through, re-check tile collision shapes and the layer/mask bit numbering, then summarize the changes and the _process caveat for the developer.
